newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-TOSHACK HOPING FOR SIGNS OF IMPROVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOSHACK HOPING FOR SIGNS OF IMPROVEMENT.

text.p: Deportivo Coruna manager John Toshack must be looking forward to Saturday's Spanish league game at struggling Extremadura if only to prove that one of the worst week's in his managerial career is over.

But the Welshman knows that the first division newcomers won't give him too much breathing space after holding leaders Real Madrid to a goalless draw at the tiny Francisco de la Hera ground just a fortnight ago.
Even so he will be happy to be playing away from the Riazor stadium.
Toshack's already rocky relationship with Deportivo fans and management took another downturn last Sunday when he insulted a section of the crowd in the game against Athletic Bilbao.
The supporters were angry that Toshack had substituted star midfielder Rivaldo, who stirred up the problem by tearing off his shirt and throwing it into the stands in disgust.
Rivaldo and Toshack pointedly ignored each other during training the following day.

Toshack has since apologised, saying that seeing footage of the game made him sweat. But he has also hit back at reporters he believes are hyper-critical by saying he will no longer hold press conferences ahead of games.
Deportivo president Augusto Lendoiro -- who took the unusual step of trying to calm both players and coach at half-time in the Bilbao game -- has begun disciplinary action against his coach.

Toshack has antagonised Lendoiro by expressing his disagreement with the club's transfer policy. And he has courted disaster with both president and fans by saying he is unlikely to continue at the end of the season.

As if that weren't enough Lendoiro is wrapped up in a legal tussle with the Spanish Federation and FIFA after appealing to the civil courts to ensure that Riazor was not closed for the game against Barcelona because of an earlier coin-throwing incident.
On the field Deportivo have lost touch with the leaders after taking just two points from three games. As a consequence Deportivo now trail Barcelona by four points and Real Madrid by seven.

On paper the game at Extremadura should be a simple task. But the bottom-placed team have shown signs of life over the past few games, and scored their first away victory last weekend against another Galician outfit, Celta Vigo.
And all the pressure will be on Toshack's men.
"If we lose (on Saturday) it could really fire things up," said Yugoslavian defender Miroslav Djukic.
